Dieter Rams, RZ 62 armchair, 1962

Dieter Rams’s lounge chair for Vitsœ: a dark glass-fibre shell of flat side panels, filled with loose upholstered cushions.

Source
Victoria and Albert Museum, CIRC.430:1-1970
Creator
Dieter Rams, designer; Vitsœ, manufacturer
Made
ca. 1962
Style
Ulm School (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Calm, restrained, solid
Evidence
Inspected the V&A’s image 2014HC8620 of object CIRC.430:1-1970 at 1600 × 1540 px, through the V&A IIIF service. The image is a black-and-white photograph, so it does not show color.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A dates the chair about 1962 and gives a black matt glass-fibre base, sides, and back, with suede-covered rubberised hair upholstery and a separate seat cushion. The record says it was manufactured by Vitsœ, Eschborn, and relaunched by Vitsœ in 2006. V&A CIRC.430:1-1970.

The same record quotes R. Hollis (1970): Rams was head of the Product Design Division at Braun AG from 1955. V&A.

Observed

  • Each side is one flat, dark panel with rounded corners. The armrest is a padded top edge that folds out over the panel.
  • Two small round bolt heads show on each side panel.
  • The seat and back are loose, square cushions with soft edges, set inside the shell.
  • The chair stands on a recessed plinth, so the body appears to float a little above the floor.

Why it belongs

The chair is the furniture branch of the style: a box of flat parts that is honest about its fixings. It is dark and upholstered, so it fits the structure and surface rules more than the white-and-grey palette.

Borrow

Show the fixings as small, regular round details instead of hiding them.
